title: How ThreadLocal works

source.title: JavaGuide (Snailclimb): Java concurrency questions (2 of 3)
source.note: Question and topic from this JavaGuide article. The answer is an original English write-up; see content/sources/javaguide/NOTICE.md.

answer: A ThreadLocal gives each thread its own value. Every Thread object has a ThreadLocalMap, and the ThreadLocal instance is the key in that map. A get looks up the current thread's map, so each thread sees only its own value. The map entries use WeakReferences to the ThreadLocal key, but the value is held strongly. That's why a leak can happen in thread pools, as covered in the next question. Typical uses are per-request user context and date formatters.

points.title: Map per thread
points.why: Each thread owns a ThreadLocalMap, so reads and writes don't need locks.

points.title: Weak key, strong value
points.why: The key is weak but the value is strong, so the value can outlive its ThreadLocal.
